plain_summary: Review contraceptive effectiveness when carbamazepine overlaps an eligible contraceptive pill or vaginal ring.

medicine_groups.name: Oral or vaginal hormonal contraceptives
medicine_groups.note: For a combination, both ingredients must belong to the same contraceptive product, in either order. A hormone replacement product does not count. A progestogen alone counts only in a regular contraceptive pill. Emergency contraception, an implant, an injection or an intrauterine system is outside this list. Examples of regular daily pills are levonorgestrel 30 micrograms and norethisterone 350 micrograms.

rule_for_models: Cite both supplies when carbamazepine overlaps a combined pill, regular progestogen-only pill or vaginal ring used to prevent pregnancy, excluding emergency tablets, HRT, intrauterine systems, implants, injections, patches and use solely for another reason. Compare the courses using the recorded directions or, if unclear, estimate cover only from a documented start and an identifiable pack schedule. Report only a possible finding if overlap or contraceptive use is unclear, asking when the patient used the pill or ring if timing is uncertain and, if reliance is unclear, “Do you rely on this pill or ring to prevent pregnancy?”
cannot_be_seen: Dispensing does not establish actual use, indication or a prescriber’s intent. Treatment and assessments elsewhere may be missing.
ask_the_gp: Could you review whether carbamazepine affects this patient’s contraceptive protection, including the need for additional protection or time-sensitive emergency contraception advice if relevant?
